eyebrow: Five ways to create a tensor
code:
import torch

a = torch.tensor([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
zeros = torch.zeros(2, 3)
ones = torch.ones(2, 3)
randn = torch.randn(2, 3)
r = torch.arange(0, 10, step=2)
caption: torch.tensor() copies your data; the others take a shape.

steps.label: device
steps.sub: cpu or cuda -- where the data physically lives

code:
a = torch.arange(12)

a.view(3, 4)
a.reshape(3, 4)
a.unsqueeze(0)   # shape (1, 12)
a.squeeze()      # drop size-1 dims
caption: reshape falls back to copying; view requires contiguous memory.

code:
a = torch.ones(3, 4)
b = torch.tensor([1., 2., 3., 4.])
c = a + b          # broadcast -> (3, 4)

x = torch.randn(3, 4)
w = torch.randn(4, 5)
y = x @ w          # matmul -> (3, 5)
caption: Elementwise ops broadcast; @ follows matrix-multiply shape rules.

subtitle: How PyTorch tracks what you do to a tensor.
